paper.title: Predicting Delays in Acute Ischemic Stroke Care with Machine Learning

claims.text: A three-layer neural network trained on four weakly associated features (duration, NIHSS severity, age, hour of day) predicts door-to-needle delay >45 min on the validation set with precision 63%, recall 67%, F1 0.64 and accuracy 60%.
The network was trained on 221 historical cases (2003-2017) and validated on a separate set of 61 cases (last 2 years).
Hyper-parameters were optimized on training and validation performance: learning rate 0.15, neurons 4/6/1, L2 lambda 0.02, 1500 iterations.
On the training set the 4/6/1 architecture gave accuracy 60%, precision 68%, recall 71%, F1 0.68.
The four features individually show only weak association with door-to-needle time (scatter/regression plots).
Application of a neural network to optimize acute care with a predictive model has not so far been reported in the literature.
The network after optimization is a 'reasonable prediction model' for stroke team performance (60% accuracy, 63% PPV).

findings.location: Methods Hyper Parameter Tuning (a) p.32370 vs bp_work/results/Output (ACCURACY 65%)
findings.evidence: The paper reports 'training-set accuracy' = 60 % (Methods Hyper Parameter Tuning (a) p.32370); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/results/Output (ACCURACY 65%)) gives 65. Our re-run gives 65.61, which matches neither.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'training-set accuracy' (60), given that bp_work/results/Output (ACCURACY 65%) gives 65?

findings.evidence: Methods: 'a regularization parameter (lambda) of 0.02 was chosen'. code/nn.py compute_cost() adds 0.002*regularizer (tf.nn.l2_loss(W1)+l2_loss(W2)+l2_loss(W3)); the factor is 0.002, ten times smaller than the stated 0.02.
findings.question_for_authors: Was lambda 0.02 or 0.002 in the run behind Table 2?

findings.evidence: The paper reports 'F1 (validation set)' = 0.64 (Table 2); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/results/predict-output.txt (F1 62%)) gives 62. Our re-run gives 65.71, which matches neither. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'F1 (validation set)' (0.64), given that bp_work/results/predict-output.txt (F1 62%) gives 62?

findings.location: Methods Hyper Parameter Tuning (a) p.32370 vs bp_work/results/Output (RECALL 69%)
findings.evidence: The paper reports 'training-set recall' = 71 % (Methods Hyper Parameter Tuning (a) p.32370); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/results/Output (RECALL 69%)) gives 69. Our re-run gives 69.17, which matches the stored output. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'training-set recall' (71), given that bp_work/results/Output (RECALL 69%) gives 69?

findings.evidence: [G2] Are inclusion/exclusion rules stated, with counts removed at each step? -> not_reported. Methods p.32368: no inclusion/exclusion counts; 221/61 split stated without the number of eligible patients
findings.question_for_authors: Are inclusion/exclusion rules stated, with counts removed at each step?

findings.evidence: [G4] Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)? -> not_reported. Methods: no outlier rule stated; code/nn.py has no filter
findings.question_for_authors: Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)?

findings.evidence: [M7] Were duplicates and near-duplicates between training and test sets removed? -> not_reported. no duplicate check between train_data.csv and test_data.csv reported
findings.question_for_authors: Were duplicates and near-duplicates between training and test sets removed?

findings.evidence:
Hyper-parameter scan (deep_checks.py): the paper says "on the validation set was assessed using the following parameters:
                                                                           b)   L2 Regularization was used to minimize overfitting wh" (l2 = 45); the code sets `0.002* regularizer` at code/nn.py:156 (l2 = 0.002). Same parameter, different value.
findings.question_for_authors: Which l2 produced the reported results, 45 or 0.002?

findings.evidence: The first line of data/test_data.csv is already data (12,74,60,3,1), but code/nn.py:16 reads it with read_csv() and the default header setting, so that observation becomes the column names. The file has 61 data lines; the code sees 60. Every count, metric and split built on this table is one row short. Same pattern at 1 more place(s): nn.py:14.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the first row of test_data.csv meant to be data? With the default header setting it is dropped.

findings.evidence: Figure 1 (scatter plots of duration, age, severity, hour vs door-to-needle time) is the only evidence for the 'weak association' of the four features, but no data file, code or numeric correlation is provided for it; the capsule contains only the 5-column csv files and the network code. The claim cannot be checked numerically.
findings.question_for_authors: Can the correlation coefficients or the plotting script for Figure 1 be provided?

findings.evidence: No random seed is reported and none is set in code/nn.py (xavier_initializer(seed=1) fixes only the initializer's internal seed; TensorFlow graph-level seed and GPU non-determinism are unset). The paper reports a single run; no variability across initialisations is given, so the stability of 63/67/0.64 is unknown.
findings.question_for_authors: Can the metrics be reported over several random initialisations (mean and range)?

findings.location: Methods, Hyper Parameter Tuning (a), p.32370 vs results/Output
findings.evidence: Paper: the 4/6/1 architecture gave on the training set 'accuracy 60%, precision 68%, recall 71%, F1 0.68'. The authors' stored training output (results/Output) prints for the training set PRECISION 68%, RECALL 69%, F1 68%, ACCURACY 65% (TP=83, TOTAL POSITIVE=122, ACTUAL POSITIVE=119, TOTAL=220). Recall 71 vs 69 and accuracy 60 vs 65 disagree; precision and F1 agree. [Capped at yellow by build_passport.py: a hand-written number finding that involves the authors' files has not passed the reproduction gate. Add the value to recomputed.json (`value` for a count made from their data, `archived` for a number read from their stored output) and re-run numbers_crosscheck.py.]
findings.question_for_authors: Which training-set metrics are correct, and on how many cases were they computed?

findings.location: Methods p.32369 ('number of neurons ... 4, 6 and 1') vs results/Output
findings.evidence: Paper states 4, 6 and 1 neurons. The stored weights in results/Output are W1 5x4, b1 5x1, W2 7x5, b2 7x1, W3 1x7, b3 1x1: the hidden layers have 5 and 7 neurons. code/nn.py sets l_z2 = l_z + l_z/2 = 7 for l_z = 5, so the code's second layer is 7, not 6; the first layer is 5 because L_Z = N = 5 columns of the csv (4 features + label column), not 4.
findings.question_for_authors: Which architecture produced the reported metrics: 4-6-1 as written, or 5-7-1 as stored?

findings.location: Methods p.32368-32369 vs data/*.csv and results/Output
findings.evidence: Paper: 221 training cases and 61 validation cases. The released files hold 220 training rows and 60 test rows (wc -l: 220 and 60 data lines plus a header line; nn.py reads them with pd.read_csv default header). The stored output prints TOTAL = 220 (training) and TOTAL = 60 (test). The paper's 221/61 equal the line counts including the header row, i.e. one more than the number of cases analysed.
findings.question_for_authors: Were 221 and 61 the case counts or the line counts of the csv files?

findings.evidence: Methods: hyper-parameters (neurons, lambda, learning rate) were 'optimized based on performance in the training and the validation sets', and the validation set is the same 60 cases on which Table 2 reports precision/recall/F1/accuracy. code/nn.py also computes the test-set cost every epoch (cost_test) and plots only the training cost. The reported validation metrics are therefore selection-set metrics, not held-out performance.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the reported validation metrics computed after hyper-parameter selection on the same 60 cases? Is there an untouched test set?

findings.evidence: 'Application of neural network in this context of optimizing acute care based on a predictive model has not so far been reported in literature' is stated without a systematic search or citation; the paper cites only four references, none a review of ML in acute stroke care.
findings.question_for_authors: On what search was the novelty statement based?

findings.evidence: 'reasonable prediction model' rests on 60% accuracy with 63% PPV on 60 cases; the base rate of delay >45 min in the validation set is 33/60 = 55% (stored output ACTUAL POSITIVE=33, TOTAL=60), so 60% accuracy is about 5 points above always predicting the majority class, and no confidence interval or comparison model is reported.
findings.question_for_authors: How does the network compare with a majority-class or logistic-regression baseline on the same 60 cases?

findings.evidence: Claim 'The network predicts door-to-needle delay >45 min on the validation set better than the majority class (accuracy above the base rate)' holds in 75% of 40 universes. Single changes that flip it: seed=4; norm=test.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the result checked under seed=4; norm=test?
